subject.title: Windows QuickStart defaults first chat to paid Anthropic model without credit warning

question: Should Anthropic QuickStart keep an Opus default with explicit paid-credit confirmation, switch first-run Anthropic to a cheaper/supported default, or only improve billing failure recovery after the first chat?
rationale: All plausible fixes change provider/default/onboarding policy, and root AGENTS.md treats setup, provider routing, defaults, and fallback behavior as compatibility-sensitive maintainer decisions.

options.title: Warn and recover around paid Opus defaults
options.body: Keep the provider default available, but add an explicit Anthropic billing/credit confirmation before terminal hatch plus clear setup-succeeded/provider-billing-failed recovery messaging.

options.title: Change the first-run Anthropic default
options.body: Select a cheaper or tester-owned Anthropic default for new QuickStart users, with upgrade-proof handling for existing configured defaults.

options.title: Document intentional Opus behavior
options.body: Leave runtime behavior unchanged and make docs/support own the paid-credit expectation, accepting that first chat can fail for unfunded Anthropic API accounts.

recommendation.title: Warn and recover around paid Opus defaults
recommendation.body: Keep the provider default available, but add an explicit Anthropic billing/credit confirmation before terminal hatch plus clear setup-succeeded/provider-billing-failed recovery messaging.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for the Anthropic default-policy choice is the commit that defaulted Anthropic to Opus, and this decision is provider/setup policy rather than a narrow code repair.
